**What the verdict rests on**
I counted only searches with a passing control. Across both rounds that is more than 30 catalogues and alert lists per candidate.

Only some of these hold 2025-26 objects, so only they could carry a report of these brightenings:
- TNS;
- AAVSO VSX, live and in VizieR's 2026-10-18 copy, which holds the 2026 novae V419 Mus and V2104 Aql;

- CBAT TOCP and the ASAS-SN transients page;
- vsnet-alert, MAXI and the Fermi-LAT nova list;
- the ATel titles and the BAA circulars;
- for A only, the ZTF brokers.

The older catalogues show only that no known variable star or earlier eruption sat at these places. They are GCVS (2020), Gaia DR3 (data to 2017), VVV (2010-19) and the nova catalogues (to 2015-22).

**Closest things found**
- Within 30 arcsec, only C has catalogued neighbours, and none is a transient or a report:
  - a Gaia RS-type star at 11.95 arcsec;
  - a VVV contact binary at 15.46 arcsec;
  - a Herschel cold-dust clump at 3.65 arcsec.
  The two stars were catalogued before 2025, are periodic, and are different stars, because C's position is good to 0.3-0.5 arcsec.
- For A and B, the nearest catalogued variables are 33.8 and 33.3 arcsec away.
- Nearest named 2025-26 events:
  - A: AT 2025qzs (a CV candidate), 37 arcmin away, and the nova AT 2026abbx, 2.56 deg away.
  - B: X-ray bursts of the known burster 4U 1705-440, 2.4 deg away.
  - C: the HP Nor dwarf-nova outburst, 3.39 deg away, and the new X-ray nova MAXI J1609-487, 3.46 deg away.

**Counted as not searched (no working control)**
- SIMBAD: CDS returned HTTP 404 at every try from 07:01 to 07:37 UTC, and the IDIA and CfA mirrors lack the 2025 control novae.
- The CBAT nova list (ends 2010), VSOLJ (last updated 2023) and, for C, the Swift/BAT list.

**Blocked**
- AAVSO alert notices (HTTP 403 for B).
- The OUP and INAF copies of Lucas et al. 2024.
- The BAA members' forum and the groups.io alert archive.

**Left for a person, searched by no one**
The full text of The Astronomer's Telegram and NASA ADS were deliberately left for a person. The first round read only ATel titles and opening lines: 942 telegrams for A, 1,217 for B and 847 for C, with V7994 Sgr found as the control. This verdict therefore records which searches ran, that they worked and what they returned; it is not proof that no one else has seen these objects. Nothing has been submitted anywhere.

**My checks**
I made no new network requests and did not open ATel or ADS. I read:
- A's 400-request log, including its four CDS 404s;
- all 31 of B's VizieR answer files: each is HTTP 200, each control was re-found at about 0 arcsec, and nothing lies nearer than 33.3 arcsec;
- C's VSX answers (V0462 Lup, V0419 Mus and V2104 Aql all present) and its VizieR summary;
- the saved robots.txt files;
- the BAA circulars VSSC 205-209.
All agree with the reports. My scripts are in <scratchpad>/referee3/scripts/

**Process notes for the team**
- aavso.org's robots.txt allows all agents in general (content signal 'use=reference'). Under a 'training crawlers' heading it disallows Anthropic's named crawlers (ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web).
  - The searchers read this differently. A made no aavso.org request, C read campaign and forum pages, and the first round queried VSX live.
  - UCL Discovery is the same case: A held back, and B read one PDF there.
- C sent two arXiv API lookups before reading that host's 'Disallow: /', and reported it.
- TNS disallows '/search/' with a slash; the first round's queries were '/search?...'.
None of these reads changes a verdict. A person can repeat them (steps 4 and 5 of the checklist) if the team wants to be strict.

**On the user's question ('the AI thing, the simulation one')**
This step ran no simulation and used no simulated or planted data. It only judged real, time-stamped requests to public services. Per the earlier ruling, four reviewers per candidate examined A, B and C in the real SPHEREx exposures. The project does have labelled simulation features: the practice screen and the planted practice round of the distant-world search, both stamped SIMULATION. Nothing from them enters these verdicts. Whether the main session is working on 'the simulation one' is for it to answer.

search:B.summary:
I found no earlier report of Candidate B in any search that worked. Nothing of any kind lies within 30 arcsec, and no named 2025-26 event lies within 5 arcmin.

What worked:
- VizieR, through the CDS mirror at CfA because CDS itself was down. I found each catalogue's identifier with VizieR's own catalogue search, then cone-searched 31 tables at 1, 10 and 60 arcmin, each with a control. The tables cover:
  - the VVV and VVVX eruptive and high-amplitude variable lists (Lucas 2017, Contreras Pena 2017 and 2019, VVV V4, VIVACE, VVV long-period variables and Miras);
  - SPICY young stars and their WISE-variability table, and NEOWISE YSO variability lists;
  - Gaia DR3 variability, the ASAS-SN variable catalogue, GCVS and the New Suspected list;
  - six nova and cataclysmic-variable catalogues.
  The nearest entries are steady stars: SPICY 43146 at 33 arcsec and a Gaia RR Lyrae star at 37 arcsec. The only nova within 1 degree is V1662 Sco (2018), 44.6 arcmin away.
- vsnet-alert: all subject lines from 2025-08 to 2026-11 (159 messages), plus 32 message bodies. Nothing in Scorpius or its neighbours is closer than 11 deg.
- MAXI: nothing new within 2 deg; the nearest entries are bursts from the known source 4U 1705-440, 2.4 deg away.
- Fermi-LAT nova list, Wikipedia's nova list, the BAA forum and its 2025-26 circulars, and open-web searches on the J-name, the Galactic name, 'Nova Sco 2025/2026' and the next Scorpius variable-star names (V1726-V1728 Sco): nothing near B.
- Guo et al. 2024 (arXiv): its nearest source is VVV-WIT-13, an eruptive young star already known before 2025, 73 arcmin away.

What did not work:
- SIMBAD at CDS was down (HTTP 404) on all five tries (07:01, 07:11, 07:19, 07:24 and 07:25 UTC), so the V462 Lup control and the 2 and 30 arcmin cones could not run. VizieR at CDS was down too.
- Lucas et al. 2024 and Guo et al. 2024 are not on VizieR. The open copy of Lucas 2024 prints only 10 of its 222 rows. The full table is behind a robot check on the publisher's site, and so are the AAVSO alert notices. INAF needs a login.
- The CBAT public nova list ends in 2010.

ATel full text and ADS were left for a person, as instructed. This is a statement about these searches, not proof that nobody has reported the object. B stays a candidate.

On the user's question ('the AI thing, the simulation one'): this step only searched published catalogues and lists. It ran no simulation and cannot say what that question refers to.

The search log is in <scratchpad>/recheck/B/searches_B_recheck.tsv, the raw answers in <scratchpad>/recheck/B/dl/ and the scripts in <scratchpad>/recheck/B/scripts/.
